Sorry for the ignorance. Is there a difference between rolling and reloading, or are they mutual terms? Also is there a subverse for learning about the process

"Rolling your own" is just slang for reloading. I actually prefer the term handloading, because there are occasions where you might be loading brand new, never before fired brass. I form cases for a couple of wildcats, mostly the 7mmTCU and .256 Winchester Magnum. In those cases, the brass may or may not have been fired before, but not as what you are forming it into.

There is a subverse on Voat, /v/handloading that I have tried to kickstart several times, but it just can't seem to get going. Sadly, on that other site that many of us came here from, there is /r/reloading that was/is very active, and I used to post a great deal there before I purged my messages and deleted my account. There are some really good discussion websites, including thefiringline.com, thehighroad.org, and handloadersbench.com that come to mind. Most powder manufacturers post their manuals online now free of charge.

Every handloader I've ever met will recommend that the very first tool you buy is a quality printed loading manual, and read the front instructional section first. Over and over, and over again until you thoroughly understand the concepts and safety points. In many communities you can find a gun shop or sporting goods store that offers classes. I plan to offer classes when I open my shop in a couple of years after retiring. And then there are always Youtube videos, which I hesitate to recommend to a newcomer because you don't yet know what you don't know, but I've learned several good tricks and techniques by watching them over the years.

And you found me, I'm here every day and happy to answer any questions you might have. I've been loading right at 40 years now, and still have all my fingers and eyes. My boss at my current job (not ammunition/firearms related) told me he hired me because in my post interview chat I mentioned that I loaded as a hobby and he noticed I still had all my parts intact and working, and that told him I was conscientious enough not to break things.

Good luck and happy handloading!
